title: Skyveil Horizon - Testing out the laser beam
author: Mindless_Software_99
selftext:
I finally got some game mechanics into the game! New enemies have been added to the world development. I also made some changes to the HUD along with introduced new mechanics such as abilities. 

This is a sneak peek into one of the characters abilities and them in action. I've already gotten interested testers. The game is getting closer to some playtesting. Let me know what you think!

I am looking for voice actors for the characters as ElevenLabs hasn't done well enough for what I am looking for. If you are interested, please comment below! Also, if you are interested in playtesting, please let me know in the comments as well.

With people who indicated interest in my last post, I am not ignoring you. I'm just hoping to get the game into a good state to conduct the testing.

comments.author: ItsDumi
comments.body:
Okay, I'm going to say this because I've seen a lot of AI effects and very few people noticing. So even tho you're not asking, these AI effects completely lack weight and layering. Look at the vfx students or pro showcases. Look at the layers, the weight. And that's often without audio, just visually.

No flame, just consider it might look good but is missing fundamentals

https://youtu.be/HTPbHeqstT0?si=qfsddo-y35Q2W8Fn

https://youtu.be/Qt4KOrRSQ3I?si=BAbSx-gVXeJouI89

replies.author: Mindless_Software_99
replies.body: Thank you for your feedback! Could you clarify what you mean? Which effects lack weight and layering? What specific elements could be improved?

replies.author: ItsDumi
replies.body:
No problem. So the weapon firing the circular beams are a little "underanimated". Just consider the basics (build up -> action -> Travel ->  Impact). If you watch the references, you'll see each on clearly has all of them (and in some cases a few more steps that are basically just repeats of the cycle on another action). 

Right now, you circle projectiles have a very very soft build up (the stars floating) and the it shoots at the npc and the it triggers with another soft collision. I see effect stacks (which actually starts bringing weight) but it also doesn't look like an intentional event. Sort of like a happy accident. You cold command that, and have it such that a stack leads to an explosion that leaves a crater for example. The regular hits could feel more "dangerous" too with a more dramatic impact.

There are steps missing in what would make the projectiles feel more like they're murdering mfers xD Exaggerate A LOT more, dramatize it make me feel like an anime superhero fucking shit up

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body:
Overall it's a good start, you're just missing the subtle pieces that make something feel like a proper game instead of a tech demo or a prototype. Someone already mentioned the VFX and I'm no VFX person so I'll skip that.

 - You need directional hit reacts and they need to be interruptible so repeated hits feel responsive when they land. As it is now the player getting hit feels like it's weak and fake.
 - The damage VO needs some more variants, and you're missing the shuffle trick games use to keep it from feeling repetitive. Take your set of clips, shuffle the whole array, ensure the end of the last shuffle and the start of the next shuffle aren't the same clip, then play through the array of VO and reshuffle when you reach the end. That'll give you a more human feeling "random" than pure random selection. 
 - You need some blending on those animation transitions. Cubic usually looks pretty good on organics, linear for machines, around 100-300ms for the transition itself. That'll help with the animation popping and jarring transitions.
 - I'd look at root motion for the locomotion, or at least syncing up your motion with foot falls since right now your characters are sliding all over the place. That makes them feel floaty and fake.

It sounds like a long list but it's mostly grunt work that I know an AI could whack out pretty quick with parallel agents. Certainly much faster than the couple months it took when I had to do all this by hand.

Edit: I just noticed the HUD is shaking in screen space on the initial charge up of the beam attack. You generally want to keep the HUD fixed and only shake the camera, moving the HUD feels like a bug unless it's embedded as part of the world itself or on the character.

replies.author: Mindless_Software_99
replies.body: Thank you, I appreciate the feedback! Yeah, the voicelines definitely need replacing. If there's any recommendations for finding voice actors, I would be interested.

replies.author: TechgeekOne
replies.body: Sadly I don't have any since that was usually someone else's job. I've had the idea of potentially doing the acting yourself then using a voice cloning model to re-speak the lines as the character voice with the same inflection and tone, but that's about the only other direction I can think of that isn't straight up hiring someone else and I've not had time to try it yet.

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: What the game development pipeline? AI model(s)?

replies.author: Mindless_Software_99
replies.body: I'm currently using Lovable for the AI coding development side (some textures and effects as well). For the design, I basically create the concepts/sprites using ChatGPT. For 3D models, I generate the concept art using ChatGPT, isolated the different components through ChatGPT and then uploaded the models to Tripo3D. For the standard characters, I generated the concept through ChatGPT, then I created a VRoid base model for the character, used Tripo3D to create their clothing and used Blender to morph the clothing to the character's body. I also used Tripo3D for rigging the NPC characters.

replies.author: sunnystormy64
replies.body: This is a good pipeline. If you have the hardware, you can sub Tripo for Pixal3D and keep your asset gen local.

comments.author: ffxivthrowaway03
comments.body:
My two biggest criticisms here:

1) This is just Temu Genshin Impact.  Like some of the models look straight ripped from Genshin.  That's not exactly an AI thing, people have been ripping off Genshin since it launched, but I urge you to find your own visual identity, there's a lot of ways to keep that stylized anime aesthetic and even go with open world adventure gameplay while differentiating yourself from Genshin.

2) The laser is excessive.  Mechanically you cannot see what you're targeting, what you're hitting, if you're even hitting anything.  It's VFX vomit that gets in the way of gameplay.  That kind of thing is fine for a quick flash, not a sustained beam you're supposed to hold for seconds at a time.  

Either way, I applaud anyone chasing the AA/AAA space and not just churning out mobile game/incremental slop.  Keep on truckin' brother, excited to see this and more games in that more ambitious development space.

replies.author: Mindless_Software_99
replies.body:
Thank you for the feedback! The base models for the characters (body, hair) were exported from VRoid Studio. The clothing was created in Tripo3D and then morphed to the character in Blender. So I guess that is sort of a compliment! But I agree, having my own visual identity would be good to do.

I definitely agree the laser is a bit much. I'll be toning it down to visually complement it with the rest of the environment.

Thank you for the support!

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
Yeah, that makes sense.  VRoid studio is pretty much an app for "I want to make a vtuber avatar that looks like it was pulled directly from Genshin" lol.  Every one of their outputs has that same exact style to it.

Get it running, then make it look good.  Good luck to you.
